# 21. Security

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Reduce static-site security risk through safe code, safe hosting, secure headers, dependency control, and secret hygiene.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A secure hosting checklist for HTTPS, TLS, redirects, DNS, access control, and deploy permissions.
- [ ] A browser security header plan covering Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, frame-ancestors, and HSTS where appropriate.
- [ ] A dependency inventory with licenses, source, version, purpose, and update policy.
- [ ] A third-party script inventory with SRI where feasible, purpose, owner, and risk review.
- [ ] A secret scanning rule for repository and deploy output.
- [ ] A form security note explaining that client-side validation is usability, not data security.
- [ ] A content injection policy for any HTML generated from Markdown, no-code export, CMS export, or client-provided content.
- [ ] A vulnerability response process for dependencies, hosting compromise, defacement, and leaked keys.

## Must Be True
- [ ] No secrets, API keys, tokens, private config, credentials, or customer data may exist in public static files.
- [ ] All production pages and assets must load over HTTPS.
- [ ] External resources must be minimized and reviewed.
- [ ] Inline scripts and styles must be avoided where a CSP will prohibit them, or explicitly nonce/hash-managed where static architecture supports it.
- [ ] User-supplied content must be sanitized before becoming static HTML.
- [ ] Admin access to hosting, DNS, analytics, form providers, and repositories must use least privilege and MFA.
- [ ] Security headers must be tested on the deployed site.
- [ ] Dependency updates must not be automatic without review when they affect production output.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check deployed headers with free header scanning tools and browser devtools.
- [ ] Check for mixed content, insecure HTTP links, target blank without noopener, and unsafe inline event handlers.
- [ ] Check repository history and deploy output for secrets, .env files, backups, source maps, and drafts.
- [ ] Check that forms do not imply secure storage unless the provider actually provides it.
- [ ] Check that external scripts are loaded only from approved domains.
- [ ] Check that CSP does not break required functionality and does block unapproved script execution.
- [ ] Check that DNS records, domain registrar, and host accounts are protected.
- [ ] Check security.txt if the organization wants a public vulnerability reporting contact.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid eval, new Function, document.write, unsafe innerHTML, inline event handlers, and untrusted HTML injection.
- [ ] Avoid exposing source maps, backups, .git folders, CMS exports, or raw design files.
- [ ] Avoid collecting sensitive data through static forms.
- [ ] Avoid using abandoned JavaScript libraries.
- [ ] Avoid loading scripts from unofficial CDNs when self-hosting is practical.
- [ ] Avoid setting security headers once and never retesting after script changes.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The site must be secure by default despite being static.
- [ ] The CSP must reflect real resource needs, not a permissive placeholder.
- [ ] Security controls must be documented so hosting can be migrated.
- [ ] Secret hygiene must apply before, during, and after launch.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the audit script for mixed content, unsafe patterns, exposed files, target blank risks, and third-party domains.
- [ ] Use generated header templates as reviewable starting points for Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages equivalents, or host dashboards.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Security strategy recognizes front-end code is public: no secrets, private files, private data, passwords, payment processing, unknown scripts, development files, or false trust.
- [ ] Repository, secrets, domain, DNS, HTTPS/TLS, hosting, deployment, headers, CSP, third-party scripts, dependencies, CDN, forms, contact links, analytics/tracking, cookies/consent, privacy/data, content, assets, external links, embeds, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, browser storage, URLs/query parameters, payments/e-commerce, downloads/files, accessibility trust, SEO safety, CMS export, backup/recovery, monitoring, incidents, QA, red flags, and final approval are checked.
- [ ] Secrets in HTML/CSS/JS/JSON/assets are treated as exposed; exposed credentials are removed and rotated.
- [ ] Forms collect only necessary data, use HTTPS endpoints, do not expose data in URLs, do not track contents, and have privacy text.
- [ ] Security rejects fake testimonials, fake badges, misleading CTAs, hidden tracking, suspicious external links, test payment links, public private files, staging indexation, and uncontrolled access.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
